## ZIP Codes (ZIP Code Tabulation Areas) {background-color="#A1D6F4"}

```{r Download and read ZIP Code Tabulation Areas}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Download and read in ZIP Code Tabulation Areas Shapefile"
#| results: "hide"

url <- "https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2025/ZCTA520/tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip"
dest_in <- "./data_in/census/TIGER2025/ZCTA520/tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip"
dest_mid <- "./data_mid/census/TIGER2025/ZCTA520/tl_2025_us_zcta520/tl_2025_us_zcta520.zip"

if(!file.exists(dest_in)) {
  dir.create(dirname(dest_in), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  curl_download(url, dest_in)
  
  dir.create(dirname(dest_mid), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  unzip(dest_in, exdir = dirname(dest_mid))
}

# Read Shapefile
zcta  <- read_sf("./data_mid/census/TIGER2025/ZCTA520/tl_2025_us_zcta520/tl_2025_us_zcta520.shp")
```

:::{.notes}
- People generally know their ZIP code, so that's nice

Any ZIP boundaries are an interpretation of ZIP Codes.

If you buy the ZIP + 4 file from the USPS, you get a table of 43 million records. Not a map.
https://postalpro.usps.com/address-quality-solutions/zip-4-product

- Cross city, county, and state boundaries

These change rapidly. The methodology is valuable to read: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/guidance/geo-areas/zctas.html

- https://about.usps.com/postal-bulletin/2009/pb22262/html/updt_002.htm

:::

## ZIP Codes - Manhattan {background-color="#A1D6F4"}

```{r Filter and plot Manhattan ZIP Codes}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code"

# Filter to New York, NY ZIP codes... sort of - Marble Hill Chopped off
zcta_manhattan <- zcta %>%
  filter(ZCTA5CE20 %in% c(as.character(seq(from = 10000, to = 10299))))

# Plot on top of Open Street Maps basemap
leaflet(zcta_manhattan) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(weight = 0.5, opacity = 1.0)
```

::: {.notes}
Skipping straight to Manhattan since the New York State ZIP Codes added 40 MB to the size of the deck

Manhattan is a nice set of territories here. A couple of notes:
- UWS side zip codes go across Central Park
- Some buildings are their own ZIP code
- Being surrounded by water helps prevent ZIP codes from spreading to other areas
- Cobble Hill is missing. It's part of a bigger ZIP code and can't be carved out

:::
